candidates.title: Plan or Retrieve First? A Scale Study of Tool Discovery Architectures
candidates.summary: Tool-augmented LLM agents discover relevant APIs from large registries before planning execution, yet finite context windows prohibit injecting all tool definitions into a single prompt. The dominant approach, which we term Retrieve-then-Plan (RtP), embeds the user query and retrieves similar tools via approximate nearest-neighbor search. We study an alternative Plan-then-Retrieve (PtR) paradigm in which the LLM first generates Abstract Tool Stubs (hypothesized function signatures describing needed capabilities) which then serve as retrieval queries against the registry. candidates.title: Smallwords: controlled-vocabulary generation with one inspectable contract
candidates.summary:
I built smallwords, a small MIT-licensed Python package for controlled-vocabulary LLM output.

The practical problem is drift. A project may describe its allowed language in a prompt, encode it again in a grammar, approximate it in JSON Schema, and then write separate validation logic. smallwords keeps one WordlistSpec at the center and derives all four surfaces from it:

  • prompt guidance
  • GBNF for constrained decoding
  • JSON Schema
  • post-generation validation
